title: What can you say about creatine in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for creatine; the strongest is "Improves performance in repeated short bursts of high-intensity exercise, such as sprints, jumps or lifting" (strong, 3-5 g a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Reverses muscle wasting or sarcopenia".

supported_wordings.wording: Improves performance in repeated short bursts of high-intensity exercise, such as sprints, jumps or lifting.
supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review, listed by Health Canada, and ODS says creatine improves performance in repeated short bursts of high-intensity activity.
supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: 3 g a day, for adults doing high-intensity exercise, and the consumer is told so. Health Canada gives three options for adults 18 and older: 3-5 g a day for at least 4 weeks with no loading phase; 15-20 g a day for 5-7 days (at most 5 g per dose) followed by 2-5 g a day; or 3-5 g a day for at least 4 weeks followed by a maintenance dose.

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims
NIH ODS fact sheet: Dietary Supplements for Exercise and Athletic Performance (health professional)

supported_wordings.wording: Helps increase lean muscle mass and size when combined with resistance training.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it; no other listed source was read on muscle mass.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: the same dose options as above. Adults 18 and older, alongside a resistance training programme.

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease state; the supported wording is about training performance and muscle mass with resistance training.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: A natural alternative to anabolic steroids
wordings_to_avoid.why: Compares the product to a drug class.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Helps with muscular dystrophy or other muscle diseases

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
